mbm-1351.clue: I let the tide keep score.
mbm-1351.quote: We drew our beach-cricket runs in the wet sand. One wave wiped out the whole record and left a neat row of shells in its place. We counted those instead and started a second innings.

mbm-1352.clue: I gave my skis an autograph.
mbm-1352.quote: After my first run down the long red slope I wrote the date on a paper luggage label and tied it to my ski bag. The ink ran in the snow, but I can still read the grin I drew.

mbm-1353.clue: I fixed the bridge before finishing the level.
mbm-1353.quote: In my favorite building game a little shopkeeper kept getting stuck on the far bank. I spent all my coins on a bridge. He finally crossed with his cart, and I forgot there was a score.

mbm-1354.clue: The mirror came with a fan.
mbm-1354.quote: I found a small mirror backed with blue enamel at a street market. The woman selling it used a paper fan to keep the glare out of my face. I paid her for both before the breeze could change.

mbm-1355.quote: At our theater I make storm clouds from old gray curtains. One has a pocket for the little bell we use for hail. Nobody in the audience knows the whole forecast hangs on my sleeve.

mbm-1356.clue: My spotter brings a pocketful of pennies.
mbm-1356.quote: I ask her to move a penny across the shelf after each lifting set. They make a tidy little row by the time I put the weights away. We spend them on the wishing fountain outside.

mbm-1357.quote: I wanted a basket for my mother’s tall knitting needles. The handle came out enormous, so I made the basket big enough for her yarn too. Now there’s even room for the book she reads between rows.

mbm-1358.quote: My curling team knotted different ribbons on our broom handles. I always look for my sister’s bright orange one across the ice when I slide out. It’s the easiest target in the whole rink.

mbm-1359.clue: I heard the museum through a shell.
mbm-1359.quote: At the natural history museum a guide let me hold a conch to my ear. Inside I heard everybody shuffling around the gallery. It might be the busiest sea I’ve ever visited.

mbm-1360.clue: I made a bench for the knights.
mbm-1360.quote: I folded an old bus timetable into a little bench beside our park chessboard. Captured pieces sit there in a queue. The match looks very dignified until my opponent calls out the next stop.

mbm-1361.clue: I make one pair of pajamas last a whole series.
mbm-1361.quote: When our show gets renewed I sew a new star onto my pajama pocket. My favorite comedy made it to five stars, and there’s barely room for a peppermint behind any of them.

mbm-1362.clue: I wrote the character who never speaks.
mbm-1362.quote: At the bus stop I saw a woman hand a stranger her umbrella without saying a word. I gave my story a character who does everything that way. Her scenes surprised me most when I read them out loud.

mbm-1363.clue: I saved a chalk drawing of a bad move.
mbm-1363.quote: My climbing partner drew my tangled-up legs on the back of a receipt. The next week I found a clean way through and he drew that too. I’ve framed them as a rather honest before and after.

mbm-1364.clue: I dance with the person holding the coats.
mbm-1364.quote: At our club somebody always gets left watching the pile. I brought a folding chair and put the coats on it. The chair has a slow evening and the rest of us finally get the same song.

mbm-1365.clue: I finish my quilt with one silver stitch.
mbm-1365.quote: My mother’s thimble has a little moon stamped on the side. When I reach the final corner I stitch a silver moon to match. You can tell exactly where I put down the needle.

mbm-1366.clue: I borrowed the club’s last paper star.
mbm-1366.quote: After the dance the owner let us take home the silver stars he’d taped around the speakers. Mine hangs over the record player. It trembles whenever I play the song we closed with.

mbm-1367.clue: I play with the sound turned up for one bird.
mbm-1367.quote: In my favorite forest game there’s a chirp just before the secret path opens. My sister can imitate it perfectly. She’s made me walk into the wrong pixel tree more than once.

mbm-1368.clue: I made the dice a soft landing.
mbm-1368.quote: Our board-game table shares a wall with a sleeping baby next door. I lined a little tray with green felt. Now we roll for kingdoms and fortunes in perfect silence.

mbm-1369.clue: I brought an empty envelope to the movies.
mbm-1369.quote: The theater was retiring its old printed program. I asked the usher to fold the final one for me. He slipped his own tiny pencil sketch of the marquee into the envelope too.

mbm-1370.clue: I drew the station cat from the credits.
mbm-1370.quote: We paused an anime’s closing shot to draw the striped cat sitting beside the luggage. My friend drew the cat’s shadow first. I drew its whiskers. Somehow ours looked like two relatives waiting for different trains.

mbm-1371.clue: I tune the snare to a teacup.
mbm-1371.quote: At rehearsal I tapped my stick against an enamel cup while the singer looked for a pitch. The little ping opened our new song. Now I put the cup on the set list along with the drums.

mbm-1372.clue: I let the smallest racer choose the car.
mbm-1372.quote: My nephew picks the silliest vehicle in our racing game, a little green bathtub on wheels. I learned every corner in that thing. The night we finally won, he fetched a rubber duck for the podium.

mbm-1373.clue: I hike with one empty picture frame.
mbm-1373.quote: I carry a little cardboard frame to the ridge and hold it up before I sketch. On my last walk a moth landed in the corner. I drew it there before I drew a single mountain.

mbm-1374.clue: I mend the elbows in two colors.
mbm-1374.quote: I patched my favorite work shirt with blue on one elbow and green on the other. My sister says she can tell which way I’ve turned in the market without seeing my face.

mbm-1375.clue: I leave room for the little one.
mbm-1375.quote: When we make arepas my brother shapes one tiny round from the last pinch of dough. We split it while the big ones cook and use its filling to decide what goes in the next batch.
